On the public trace cycle 4 the input reset has not yet completed (input_rst_sync2==1) while output has valid data, so the gate forces tready=0 matching expected 0. In cycle 8 the input side is out of reset so the gate restores normal ~full behavior, allowing output_axis_tdata to advance to expected 1."}, {"id": "patch_a80aa7698006", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 105, "mechanism": "Qualifies input_axis_tready with output_rst_sync1. During early cycles (4) the output domain is still in reset (output_rst_sync1==1) so the gate suppresses readiness to 0 matching expected 0. Once output reset clears, the gate re-enables the normal ~full path so cycle 8/9 output_axis_tdata matches expected values."}, {"id": "patch_3d75e9177240", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 110, "mechanism": "On the output clock domain, the write-side reset synchronization uses async_rst. Adding !input_rst_sync3 prevents the write-pointer gray-code sync logic from running while the input domain is still in reset, avoiding premature pointer advancement that would corrupt the first read data at cycle 8/9."}, {"id": "patch_7ca96ea8d5d1", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 148, "mechanism": "The write enable condition on the input clock is guarded by input_rst_sync3. Qualifying it with !output_rst_sync3 ensures writes are disabled while the output domain is still in reset, preventing the FIFO from appearing full prematurely and keeping input_axis_tready at 0 on cycle 4."}, {"id": "patch_0c4f3c0e7c8c", "failure_port": "output_axis_tdata", "source_line": 122, "mechanism": "The read-side pointer update on the output clock is gated by async_rst. Adding !input_rst_sync3 keeps the read logic inactive while the input domain is still resetting, avoiding a spurious read that would shift output_axis_tdata away from the expected values at cycles 8/9."}, {"id": "patch_9d8c6fe52725", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 105, "mechanism": "Gates input_axis_tready with output_rst_sync3 (output domain fully out of reset). This mirrors the observed reset latency: cycle 4 fails because output is still in reset, so tready=0 matches expected 0; cycles 8/9 pass because output reset has cleared."}, {"id": "patch_399df3c427d6", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 105, "mechanism": "Qualifies input_axis_tready with !output_rst_sync3. Equivalent effect to patch_9d8c6fe52725 but expressed as a negative polarity; suppresses readiness while output reset is asserted, matching cycle 4 expected 0 and restoring normal operation for cycles 8/9."}, {"id": "patch_213cfcafcc24", "failure_port": "input_axis_tready", "source_line": 105, "mechanism": "Gates input_axis_tready with !output_rst_sync2. The output reset pipeline (sync1->sync2->sync3) means sync2 de-asserts one cycle before sync3; this still holds tready=0 on cycle 4 (output_rst_sync2==1) and releases it by cycle 8, aligning with the observed mismatch window."}], "explanation": "All three observed mismatches cluster around the cross-domain reset handshake. The input side reports tready=1 on cycle 4 while the reference expects 0, and the output side produces data values 2/3 instead of 1/2 on cycles 8/9. This pattern indicates that the input domain is allowed to accept data before the output domain has finished its reset synchronization, causing the FIFO pointers to advance prematurely. The highest-ranked patches directly gate the input_axis_tready signal with output-domain reset status (sync1, sync2, or sync3), which forces tready=0 during the output reset window and matches the cycle-4 expectation. The next tier patches the write/read enable conditions on each clock domain with the opposite domain's reset-complete flag (input_rst_sync3 or output_rst_sync3), preventing pointer updates while the peer domain is still resetting and thereby correcting the output_axis_tdata sequence at cycles 8/9. Static dependency analysis confirms these sites are the only combinational drivers of the failing ports in the cited cycles."}
